translations.literal: Under Duke of Haixi in Taihe years Shanyin county in Kuaiji raised a granary; digging earth they obtained two great boats full of cash—the coins all large with rim script.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi era: digging a granary at Shanyin yielded two treasure boats of large rimmed coins.

sentences.zh: 時日向暮，鑿者馳以告官，官夜遣防守甚嚴。

translations.literal: The sun was setting; diggers galloped to report to officials; officials by night posted guard very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk fell; diggers raced to magistrates who sealed the site by night.

sentences.zh: 至明旦，失錢所在，惟有船存。

translations.literal: By dawn the cash’s whereabouts were gone—only the boats remained.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn came—the coins had vanished, boats left empty.

sentences.zh: 視其狀，悉有錢處。

translations.literal: Observing their condition, everywhere coins had been showed marks.
translations.idiomatic: Hull scars showed where coin had lain.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙初，東陽太守殷仲文照鏡不見其頭，尋亦誅翦，占與甘卓同也。

translations.literal: At the start of Andi’s Yixi era Yin Zhongwen, prefect of Dongyang, looked in the mirror and did not see his head; soon he was executed and cut down—the omen matched Gan Zhuo’s.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi early: Yin Zhongwen’s mirror showed no head—soon executed like Gan Zhuo.

translations.literal: Equals sign used as a typographical section divider.
translations.idiomatic: Typographical section divider.

sentences.zh: 水

translations.literal: Water.
translations.idiomatic: Water.

sentences.zh: =《傳》曰：「簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。」

translations.literal: =The Tradition says: “If one neglects ancestral temples, does not pray at shrines, abandons sacrifices, and violates Heaven’s seasons—then water does not soak downward.”
translations.idiomatic: Neglect shrines, skip sacrifice, defy the seasons—water will not sink to nourish.

sentences.zh: 說曰：水，北方，終藏萬物者也。

translations.literal: The explanation says: Water is the north; it stores away the myriad things at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Water is north—the force that seals creation away.

sentences.zh: 其於人道，命終而形藏，精神放越。

translations.literal: As for human way: life ends and form is stored away; spirit and soul scatter.
translations.idiomatic: For humanity it means death hiding the body while spirit wanders.

sentences.zh: 聖人為之宗廟，以收魂氣，春秋祭祀，以終孝道。

translations.literal: Sages made ancestral temples to gather soul-breath; spring and autumn sacrifices to fulfill filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sages built shrines to gather souls and seasonal rites to finish filial love.

sentences.zh: 王者即位，必郊祀天地，禱祈神祇，望秩山川，懷柔百神，亡不宗事。

translations.literal: When the kingly person mounts the throne he must suburban-sacrifice Heaven and Earth, pray to spirits, scan-ranked mountains and rivers, soothe the hundred spirits—none go unhonored in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Accession brings suburban rites to Heaven and Earth, prayers to gods, offerings to every peak and stream.

sentences.zh: 慎其齋戒，致其嚴敬，是故鬼神歆饗，多獲福助。

translations.literal: Careful in purification and abstinence, utmost in solemn reverence—therefore ghosts and spirits relish the offerings and much blessing aid is gained.
translations.idiomatic: Pure vigil and solemn awe win spirits’ favor.

sentences.zh: 此聖王所以順事陰氣，和神人也。

translations.literal: This is how sage kings comply with yin qi and harmonize spirits and men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus sage kings align with yin and join gods and mortals.

sentences.zh: 及至發號施令，亦奉天時。

translations.literal: When it comes to issuing commands, they likewise obey Heaven’s seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Their edicts too heed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 十二月咸得其氣，則陰陽調而終始成。

translations.literal: When the twelve months each obtain their qi, yin and yang are tuned and completion runs from end to beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve months in harmony—yin and yang complete the cycle.

sentences.zh: 如此，則水得其性矣。

translations.literal: Thus water obtains its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Then water keeps its nature.

sentences.zh: 若乃不敬鬼神，政令逆時，水失其性。

translations.literal: But if ghosts and spirits are not revered and government orders violate the seasons—water loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Spurn spirits and twist policy against the seasons—water loses its way.

sentences.zh: 霧水暴出，百川逆溢，壞鄉邑，溺人民，及淫雨傷稼穡，是為水不潤下。

translations.literal: Fog-waters burst forth, hundred streams rebel and overflow, ruin villages and towns, drown the people, and excessive rain harms sowing and reaping—this is water not soaking downward.
translations.idiomatic: Flash floods, rivers reversing, towns drowned, endless rains spoiling crops—that is water refusing to soak downward.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「顓事者加，誅罰絕理，厥災水。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Yi Commentary says: “When specialists on affairs increase, punishments cut off principle—its calamity is water.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang: skewed offices and cruel justice bring water’s scourge.

sentences.zh: 其水也，雨，殺人，以隕霜，大風天黃。

translations.literal: As for its water: rain, kills people; together with falling frost; great wind and heaven yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Its form: deadly rains, killing frost, yellow skies and gales.

sentences.zh: 饑而不損，茲謂泰，厥大水，水殺人。

translations.literal: Famine yet no diminution—this is called excess—its great flood; water kills people.
translations.idiomatic: Famine without relent is arrogance—great floods drown the people.

sentences.zh: 避遏有德，茲謂狂，厥水，水流殺人也。

translations.literal: Blocking those with virtue—this is called madness—its flood—flowing water kills people.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing the worthy is frenzy—rivers kill.

sentences.zh: 已水則地生蟲。

translations.literal: When water ends then on earth worms are born.
translations.idiomatic: After the flood insects breed in the soil.

sentences.zh: 歸獄不解，茲謂追非，厥水寒，殺人。

translations.literal: Returning guilt without resolving—this is called pursuing wrong—its water cold, kills people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaping blame without mercy brings icy killing rains.

sentences.zh: 追誅不解，茲謂不理，厥水五穀不收。

translations.literal: Pursuing executions without resolving—this is called not governing—its water, the five grains do not harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Endless executions mean misrule—the five grains fail.

sentences.zh: 大敗不解，茲謂皆陰，厥水流入國邑，隕霜殺穀。

translations.literal: Great defeat without resolving—this is called all yin—its water flows into the state and city; falling frost kills grain.
translations.idiomatic: Total rout unhealed—pure yin—waters flood the capital; frost kills the crop.

sentences.zh: 」董仲舒曰：「交兵結仇，伏屍流血，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛，故大水也。」

translations.literal: ” Dong Zhongshu said: “When arms cross and hatred binds, corpses lie and blood flows, the hundred clans grieve and resent—yin qi flourishes—therefore great water.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu adds: war breeds feud, corpses litter the ground, the people groan—yin swells—so come the floods.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝六月，大雨霖，伊洛溢，至津陽城門，漂數千家，殺人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Wei Wendi great prolonged rain fell; Yi and Luo overflowed to Jinyang Gate—several thousand households were swept away and people killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Wen’s sixth month brought ceaseless rain; the Yi and Luo poured through Jinyang Gate, washing away thousands of homes.

sentences.zh: 初，帝即位，自鄴遷洛，營造宮室，而不起宗廟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor mounted the throne he moved from Ye to Luoyang and built palace chambers but did not raise ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he moved the court from Ye to Luoyang, lavishing palaces while erecting no ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 太祖神主猶在鄴，嘗於建始殿饗祭如家人禮，終黃初不復還鄴。

translations.literal: Taizu’s spirit tablet remained at Ye; he once offered feast-sacrifice at Jianshi Hall like family ritual—throughout Huangchu he never returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His father’s tablet stayed in Ye while he feasted the dead like a private household in Jianshi Hall—never restoring proper site through the Huangchu era.

sentences.zh: 又郊社神祇，未有定位。

translations.literal: Moreover suburban and soil-altar spirits had no fixed placement.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-and-earth spirits lacked fixed stations at the suburban shrines.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for neglecting ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s sentence for shrines scanted and offerings abandoned.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權夏，茶陵縣鴻水溢出，漂二百餘家。

translations.literal: Under Wu Sun Quan in summer Chaling county Hong water overflowed and drifted more than two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's reign: the Hong torrent burst Chaling county and swept away two hundred homes.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋，丹陽、故鄣等縣又鴻水溢出。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year's autumn Danyang and Guchang counties again had Hong water overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn of the thirteenth year: Danyang and Guchang saw the same flood surge.

sentences.zh: 案權稱帝三十年，竟不於建鄴創七廟。

translations.literal: According to Sun Quan, thirty years titled emperor, to the end did not establish seven temples at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ruled three decades as emperor yet never founded the seven royal shrines at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 惟父堅一廟遠在長沙，而郊祀禮闕。

translations.literal: Only father Jian's single temple lay far in Changsha, while suburban sacrifice rites were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sun Jian's lone shrine stood distant in Changsha; suburban worship stayed neglected.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾初，群臣奏宜郊祀，又不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiahe ministers memorialized that suburban sacrifice was fitting—again he did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiahe ministers urged suburban rites—Sun Quan refused.

sentences.zh: 末年雖一南郊，而北郊遂無聞焉。

translations.literal: In late years although once southern suburban, northern suburban thereafter went unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he performed one southern suburban rite but never paired it with the northern altar.

sentences.zh: 吳楚之望亦不見秩，反祀羅陽妖神，以求福助。

translations.literal: The Wu-Chu peak sacrifices were also not given ranked offerings; instead they sacrificed to Luoyang demon spirits to seek blessing aid.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped ranked sacrifices to the great peaks and worshipped freak gods at Luoyang for luck.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，權簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，故示此罰，欲其感悟也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say Quan neglected ancestral temples, did not pray at shrines, abandoned sacrifices—therefore showed this punishment, desiring him to awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned: shrines scanted, prayers neglected, offerings dropped—the floods were meant to wake him.

sentences.zh: ，吳又有大風湧水之異。

translations.literal: , Wu again had prodigy of great wind and surging water.
translations.idiomatic: Wu also saw gales and walls of water.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權南郊，宜是鑒咎徵乎！

translations.literal: That winter Quan performed southern suburban—ought this to mirror the ill omen?
translations.idiomatic: That winter he offered the southern suburban—perhaps answering the prior portent.

sentences.zh: 還而寢疾，明年四月薨。

translations.literal: Returning he fell bedridden; the next year fourth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He took ill on his return and died the next spring.

sentences.zh: 一曰，權時信納譖訴，雖陸遜勳重，子和儲貳，猶不得其終，與漢安帝聽讒免楊震、廢太子同事也。

translations.literal: One interpretation: Quan then trusted accepting slander—though Lu Xun's merit was weighty and son He was heir, still they did not obtain good end—same affair as Han Andi listening to slander dismissing Yang Zhen and deposing heir.
translations.idiomatic: Some blame Sun Quan's taste for slander—Lu Xun and heir Sun He ruined like Han Andi's purge of Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 且赤烏中無年不用兵，百姓愁怨。

translations.literal: Moreover in the Chiwu years there was no year without using troops—the hundred clans grieved and resented.
translations.idiomatic: The Chiwu era knew war every year and endless popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，將軍馬茂等又圖逆。

translations.literal: In the eighth year's autumn generals Ma Mao and others again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ma Mao and fellow officers plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝九月，淫雨，冀、兗、徐、豫四州水出，沒溺殺人，漂失財產。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Wei Mingdi excessive rain—Ji, Yan, Xu, Yu four provinces sent forth water, drowned and killed people, drifted and lost property.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Ming's ninth month: soaking rains drowned Ji, Yan, Xu, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 帝自初即位，便淫奢極欲，多占幼女，或奪士妻，崇飾宮室，妨害農戰，觸情恣欲，至是彌甚，號令逆時，饑不損役。

translations.literal: From the emperor's first mounting the throne he indulged extravagance and utmost desire, seized many young girls, sometimes seized scholar-officials' wives, adorned palace chambers, harmed farming and warfare, followed emotion and wanton desire—to here gradually worse; orders violated seasons; famine yet labor not reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Since accession he hoarded girls, seized wives, lavished palaces, crippled farming and defense—commands ran against the seasons while famine raged and corvée never eased.

sentences.zh: 此水不潤下之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of water not soaking downward.
translations.idiomatic: That is water refusing to nourish below.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮夏，大水。

translations.literal: Under Wu Sun Liang in summer great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang's summer brought catastrophic flooding.

sentences.zh: 亮即位四年，乃立權廟。

translations.literal: Four years after Liang's mounting the throne he established Quan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Four years into his reign Sun Liang finally built a shrine for Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 又終吳世不上祖宗之號，不修嚴父之禮，昭穆之數有闕。

translations.literal: Moreover through the Wu age they never elevated ancestor titles or cultivated stern-father rites—the zhaomu sequence had gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wu's reign they never titled the ancestors or performed full father rites—the shrine ranks stayed broken.

sentences.zh: 亮及休、皓又並廢二郊，不秩群神。

translations.literal: Liang and Xiu and Hao together abolished the two suburban sacrifices and did not rank the host of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang, Sun Xiu, and Sun Hao each scrapped both suburb sacrifices and left gods unordered.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟不祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for neglecting ancestral temples and not sacrificing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished neglected shrines and empty altars.

sentences.zh: 又，是時孫峻專政，陰勝陽之應乎！

translations.literal: Moreover at this time Sun Jun monopolized government—is this yin overcoming yang's response!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun's dictatorship matched yin overwhelming yang.

sentences.zh: 孫休五月，大雨，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: Under Sun Xiu in the fifth month great rain; springs welled and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's fifth month: downpours until springs burst their banks.

sentences.zh: 昔歲作浦裏塘，功費無數，而田不可成，士卒死叛，或自賊殺，百姓愁怨，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: The previous year they built the Pulitang project—expense without limit yet fields could not be completed; soldiers died or rebelled or killed one another; the hundred clans grieved and resented—yin qi flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The costly Pulitang canal brought only waste fields, mutinous troops, and popular despair—yin rose thick.

sentences.zh: 休又專任張布，退盛沖等，吳人賊之應也。

translations.literal: Xiu again trusted Zhang Bu exclusively and dismissed Sheng Chong and others—this was Wu people's suffering response.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu relied solely on Zhang Bu and cashiered Sheng Chong—the people of Wu paid the price.

sentences.zh: 五年八月壬午，大雨震電，水泉湧溢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year's eighth month renwu day great rain, lightning, springs welled and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, eighth month, renwu: thunder, cloudbursts, and boiling springs.

sentences.zh: 武帝九月，青、徐、兗、豫四州大水。

translations.literal: Under Wudi in the ninth month Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu four provinces had great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's ninth month: Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu drowned.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，大雨霖，河、洛、伊、沁皆溢，殺二百餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year's sixth month great prolonged rain—He, Luo, Yi, and Qin all overflowed and killed more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, sixth month: the He, Luo, Yi, and Qin rivers burst their banks, killing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 自帝即尊位，不加三后祖宗之號。

translations.literal: From the emperor's assuming honored position he did not add titles for the three empresses and ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Since enthronement he gave no posthumous ranks to the three empresses or forebears.

sentences.zh: 又除明堂南郊五帝座，同稱昊天上帝，一位而已。

translations.literal: Moreover he removed the Ming Hall southern suburban five emperor seats, unifying the title as Haotian Shangdi—a single seat only.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped the Ming Hall of the five polar gods and collapsed worship into one Haotian seat.

sentences.zh: 又省先-{后}-配地之祀。

translations.literal: Moreover he omitted sacrifice matching former empress to earth.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the rite pairing the late empress with Earth.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰也。

translations.literal: This was punishment for neglecting ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sentence for shrines scanted and offerings abandoned.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年九月，徐州大水。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning, ninth month, Xuzhou great water.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning year one, ninth month: Xuzhou floods.

sentences.zh: 二年七月癸亥，河南、魏郡暴水，殺百餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year's seventh month guihai day Henan and Weijun storm water killed more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, seventh month, guihai: Henan and Wei commanderies drowned a hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 閏月，荊州郡國五大水，流四千餘家。

translations.literal: Intercalary month Jingzhou commanderies and kingdoms five great water—four thousand and more families drifted.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month: five Jingzhou jurisdictions lost four thousand households to the torrent.

sentences.zh: 去年采擇良家子女，露面入殿，帝親簡閱，務在姿色，不訪德行，有蔽匿者以不敬論，搢紳愁怨，天下非之，陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: The previous year they gathered daughters of good families, exposed faces entering the hall—the emperor personally inspected, aiming only at beauty and not visiting virtue; those who concealed faced trial as disrespect—gentry grieved and resented; all under Heaven condemned—yin flourishing response.
translations.idiomatic: Palace draft chose women by face alone; hiding beauty earned indictment—the elite groaned and yin energies swelled.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，益、梁二州郡國八暴水，殺三百餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year's sixth month Yi and Liang two provinces' eight commanderies storm water killed more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, sixth month: Yi and Liang lost eight counties and three hundred lives.

sentences.zh: 七月，荊州大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jingzhou great water.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Jingzhou inundated.

sentences.zh: 九月，始平郡大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shiping commandery great water.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Shiping commandery flooded.

sentences.zh: 十月，青、徐、兗、豫、荊、益、梁七州又大水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, Yi, Liang seven provinces again great water.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: seven provinces from Qing to Liang flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是時賈充等用事專恣，而正人疏外者多，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: At this time Jia Chong and others wielded affairs exclusively and wantonly while upright men were mostly cast aside—yin qi flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's clique ran riot while honest officials sat outside—yin dominated.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，司、冀、兗、豫、荊、揚郡國二十大水，傷秋稼，壞屋室，有死者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year's seventh month Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Yang commanderies and kingdoms twenty great water—harmed autumn crops, ruined houses, there were dead.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, seventh month: twenty jurisdictions from Si to Yang drowned crops and homes.

sentences.zh: 六月，泰山、江夏大水，泰山流三百家，殺六十餘人，江夏亦殺人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Taishan and Jiangxia great water—Taishan drifted three hundred households, killed more than sixty; Jiangxia also killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Taishan and Jiangxia surged—three hundred Taishan homes gone, sixty dead; Jiangxia too took lives.

sentences.zh: 時平吳後，王浚為元功而詆劾妄加，荀、賈為無謀而並蒙重賞，收吳姬五千，納之後宮，此其應也。

translations.literal: At the time after pacifying Wu Wang Jun was chief merit yet slander struck him wantonly; Xun and Jia were without counsel yet together received heavy reward; gathered five thousand Wu concubines and inducted them into the rear palace—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Peace with Wu brought Wang Jun slandered, Xun and Jia rewarded without merit, and five thousand Wu women swept into the harem—the floods answered that hubris.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，兗州大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth year's seventh month Yanzhou great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, seventh month: Yanzhou flood.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河南及荊、揚六州大水。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Henan and Jing, Yang six provinces great water.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Henan plus six provinces from Jing to Yang drowned.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，郡國四大水，又隕霜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year's ninth month four commanderies and kingdoms great water—again falling frost.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, ninth month: four jurisdictions flooded and frost fell.

sentences.zh: 是月，南安等五郡大水。

translations.literal: That month Nan'an and other five commanderies great water.
translations.idiomatic: Same month: Nan'an circuit and five commanderies inundated.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，郡國十大水，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year's fourth month ten commanderies and kingdoms great water—ruined cottages.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, fourth month: ten jurisdictions wrecked farmsteads.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，郡國八大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh year's ninth month eight commanderies and kingdoms great water.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, ninth month: eight jurisdictions underwater.

sentences.zh: 八月六月，郡國八大水。

translations.literal: Eighth month, sixth month, eight commanderies and kingdoms great water.
translations.idiomatic: The text's corrupted date still records another wave of flooding in eight jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 惠帝，有水災。

translations.literal: Under Huidi there were water disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui's reign brought repeated inundations.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，潁川、淮南大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth year's fifth month Yingchuan and Huainan great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, fifth month: Yingchuan and Huainan flooded.

sentences.zh: 六月，城陽、東莞大水，殺人，荊、揚、徐、兗、豫五州又水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chengyang and Dongguan great water—killed people; Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu five provinces again water.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Chengyang and Dongguan drowned people; Jing, Yang, Xu, Yan, and Yu flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是時帝即位已五載，猶未郊祀，其蒸嘗亦多不親行事。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had mounted the throne five years yet still not performed suburban sacrifice; the steamed offerings also many times were not personally conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Five years on the throne he still skipped suburban worship and often sent substitutes to seasonal feasts.

sentences.zh: 此簡宗廟廢祭祀之罰。

translations.literal: This was punishment for neglecting ancestral temples and abandoning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished shrines neglected and offerings abandoned.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，刑、揚二州大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth year's fifth month Jing and Yang two provinces great water.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, fifth month: the Jing and Yang circuits drowned.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后亂朝，寵樹賈、郭，女主專政，陰氣盛之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia disrupted the court, favored and planted Jia and Guo, the female ruler dominated government—yin flourishing response.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia's faction ruled through female favorites—yin's surge.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，金墉城井溢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year's fifth month Jinyong fortress well overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year, fifth month: Jinyong's well boiled over.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》，成帝時有此妖，後王莽僭逆。

translations.literal: The Han Treatise: during Emperor Cheng this prodigy appeared; afterward Wang Mang usurped.
translations.idiomatic: Han records match Chengdi's well omen with Wang Mang's usurpation.

sentences.zh: 今有此妖，趙王倫篡位，倫廢帝於此城，井溢所在，其天意也。

translations.literal: Now having this prodigy, Prince Zhao Lun usurped—Lun deposed the emperor at this fortress; where the well overflowed lies Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The same sign preceded Sima Lun's coup—the deposed emperor sat in Jinyong where the water rose.

sentences.zh: 九月，荊、揚、徐、冀、豫五州大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jing, Yang, Xu, Ji, Yu five provinces great water.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: five provinces from Jing to Yu submerged.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后暴戾滋甚，韓謐驕猜彌扇，卒害太子，旋以禍滅。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Jia's violent cruelty grew worse; Han Mi's arrogance and suspicion fanned wider—finally harmed the heir; soon destroyed by calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nanfeng turned brutal, Han Mi grew vicious—the heir died and they followed.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，宮中井水沸溢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year's fourth month palace well water boiled and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, fourth month: palace wells gushed.

sentences.zh: 永甯元年七月，南陽、東海大水。

translations.literal: In Yongning first year's seventh month Nanyang and Donghai great water.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning year one, seventh month: Nanyang and Donghai floods.

sentences.zh: 是時齊王冏專政，陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Qi Sima Jiong monopolized government—yin flourishing response.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong's dictatorship showed yin ascendant.

sentences.zh: 七月，兗、豫、徐、冀四州水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yan, Yu, Xu, Ji four provinces water.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Yan, Yu, Xu, and Ji awash.

sentences.zh: 時將相力政，無尊主心，陰盛故也。

translations.literal: At this time generals and ministers struggled for power with no heart to honor the sovereign—yin flourishing therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords feuded with no loyalty to the throne—again yin rising.

sentences.zh: 孝懷帝四月，江東大水。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Huai in the fourth month Jiangdong great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai's fourth month drowned east of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 時王導等潛懷翼戴之計，陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dao and others secretly harbored the plan to support enthronement—yin flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao's circle plotted a new emperor—another yin tide.

sentences.zh: 元帝六月，大水。

translations.literal: Under Yuandi in the sixth month great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's sixth month: widespread flood.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦內懷不臣，傲很陵上，此陰氣盛也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun inwardly harbored no minister's heart, arrogant and cruel overbearing superiors—this was yin flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun nursed treason and bullied the court—yin ruled.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，又大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth year's seventh month again great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, seventh month: floods returned.

sentences.zh: 五月，荊州及丹陽、宣城、吳興、壽春大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jingzhou and Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Shouchun great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: Jingzhou and four eastern commanderies flooded.

sentences.zh: 明帝五月，丹陽、宣城、吳興、壽春大水。

translations.literal: Under Mingdi in the fifth month Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Shouchun great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's fifth month repeated the eastern inundations.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦威權震主，陰氣盛故也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun's awe-inspiring authority shook the sovereign—yin flourishing therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's terror tactics cowed the emperor—yin still dominant.

sentences.zh: 成帝五月，大水。

translations.literal: Under Chengdi in the fifth month great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng's fifth month: deluge.

sentences.zh: 是時嗣主幼沖，母后稱制，庾亮以元舅決事禁中，陰勝陽故也。

translations.literal: At this time the heir was young and weak, mother empress held regency, Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle decided affairs within the palace—yin overcoming yang therefore.
translations.idiomatic: A child throne, empress regent, Yu Liang ruling from the harem—yin eclipsed yang.

sentences.zh: 二年五月戊子，京都大水。

translations.literal: In the second year's fifth month wuzi day capital great water.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, fifth month, wuzi: the capital drowned.

sentences.zh: 是冬，以蘇峻稱兵，都邑塗地。

translations.literal: That winter because Su Jun raised troops the capital was mud-smeared.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Su Jun's revolt left the capital in ashes and mud.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，丹陽、宣城、吳興、會稽大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth year's seventh month Danyang, Xuancheng, Wuxing, Kuaiji great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, seventh month: the lower Yangzi basin flooded.

sentences.zh: 是冬，郭默作亂，荊豫共討之，半歲乃定，兵役之應也。

translations.literal: That winter Guo Mo rebelled; Jing and Yu jointly campaigned—half a year before pacified—military labor response.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo's winter rebellion took Jing and Yu half a year to crush—war's echo.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh year's fifth month great water.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, fifth month: flood.

sentences.zh: 是時帝未親機務，政在大臣，陰勝陽也。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had not personally handled policy—affairs lay with great ministers—yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed clear of statecraft—ministers held yin sway.

sentences.zh: 八月，長沙、武陵大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Changsha and Wuling great water.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: Changsha and Wuling submerged.

sentences.zh: 穆帝五月，大水。

translations.literal: Under Mudi in the fifth month great water.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu's fifth month: inundation.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth year's fifth month great water.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, fifth month: flood.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，又大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth year's fifth month again great water.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, fifth month: floods again.

sentences.zh: 時幼主沖弱，母后臨朝，又將相大臣各執權政，與咸和初同事也。

translations.literal: At this time the young sovereign was weak, mother empress faced court, moreover generals and great ministers each grasped power—same affair as Xianhe's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Another child ruler, another regent, another crop of strongmen—like Xianhe's opening years.

sentences.zh: 七年七月甲辰夜，濤水入石頭，死者數百人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year's seventh month jiachen night tidal water entered Shitou—several hundred dead.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, seventh month, jiachen night: a bore swept Shitou fort—hundreds drowned.

sentences.zh: 是時殷浩以私忿廢蔡謨，遐邇非之。

translations.literal: At this time Yin Hao out of private resentment dismissed Cai Mo—far and near condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao cashiered Cai Mo from spite—the realm jeered.

sentences.zh: 又幼主在上而殷桓交惡，選徒聚甲，各崇私權，陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: Moreover the young sovereign above while Yin and Huan turned hostile—raised troops, gathered armor, each exalted private power—yin overcoming yang response.
translations.idiomatic: Child on the throne; Yin Hao and Huan Wen feuded—hosts mobilized for private ends.

sentences.zh: 一說，濤水入石頭，以為兵占。

translations.literal: One interpretation: tidal water entering Shitou was taken as military omen.
translations.idiomatic: Some read the Shitou tide as an omen of war.

sentences.zh: 是後殷浩、桓溫、謝尚、荀羨連年征伐，百姓愁怨也。

translations.literal: Afterward Yin Hao, Huan Wen, Xie Shang, and Xun Xian campaigned year after year—the hundred clans grieved and resented.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, Huan Wen, Xie Shang, and Xun Xian kept the realm at war until the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month brought another deluge.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，又大水。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year again great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year’s fourth month flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫權制朝廷，專征伐，陰勝陽也。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen controlled the court by power and specialized in campaigns—yin overcame yang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen hijacked the government for foreign wars—yin eclipsed yang.

sentences.zh: 海西六月，京師大水，平地數尺，浸及太廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month under Duke of Haixi the capital had great flood—several chi on level ground—submerged to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi’s sixth month drowned the capital knee-deep and lapped the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 硃雀大航纜斷，三艘流入大江。

translations.literal: The Scarlet Bird pontoon cables snapped; three vessels drifted into the great river.
translations.idiomatic: The Vermilion Bird bridge parted; three hulls washed into the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 丹陽、晉陵、吳郡、吳興、臨海五郡又大水，稻稼蕩沒，黎庶饑饉。

translations.literal: Danyang, Jinling, Wu commandery, Wuxing, and Linhai five commanderies again had great flood—rice crops washed away, commoners starved.
translations.idiomatic: Five eastern commanderies flooded again; grain vanished and famine spread.

sentences.zh: 初，四年桓溫北伐敗績，十喪其九，五年又征淮南，逾歲乃克，百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year Huan Wen’s northern campaign was defeated and lost nine of ten; in the fifth year he again campaigned Huainan and took over a year to conquer—response of the hundred clans grieving.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen’s failed northern thrust and grinding Huainan war answered popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝十二月壬午，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: On renwu day in the twelfth month of Emperor Jianwen tidal water entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen’s twelfth month, renwu day: the bore reached Shitoe.

sentences.zh: 明年，妖賊盧竦率其屬數百人入殿，略取武庫三庫甲仗，遊擊將軍毛安之討滅之，兵興、陰盛之應也。

translations.literal: The next year bandit Lu Song led several hundred followers into the hall, seized armor from three armory vaults; guerrilla general Mao Anzhi campaigned and destroyed them—response of armies rising and yin flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Song raided the palace armory; Mao Anzhi crushed him—another war omen.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝六月，大水。

translations.literal: Under Xiaowudi in the sixth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu’s sixth month: floods.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼弱，政在將相。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was young and weak; policy lay with generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: A boy emperor left policy to generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: inundation.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，揚、荊、江三州大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yang, Jing, and Jiang three provinces great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Yang, Jing, and Jiang drowned.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，始興、南康、廬陵大水，平地五丈。

translations.literal: In the eighth year’s third month Shixing, Nankang, and Luling great flood—five zhang on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, eighth year: western commanderies stood fifteen feet under water.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the tenth year’s fifth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year, fifth month: flood.

sentences.zh: 自八年破苻堅後，有事中州，役無寧歲，愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: From the eighth year after defeating Fu Jian there were affairs in the Central Plains—labor never knew a peaceful year—response of grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns on the Central Plain never ceased after Feishui—popular anger answered in rain.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，濤水入石頭，毀大航，殺人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year’s December tidal water entered Shitou, destroyed the great bridge, killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth year: Shitou tide snapped the great pontoon and killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，慕容氏寇擾司兗，鎮戍西北，疲於奔命，愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: The next year Murong raiders harassed Si and Yan; northwest garrisons exhausted running errands—response of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Murong incursions wore out the northwest—Heaven echoed with floods.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月，沔中諸郡及兗州大水。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year’s seventh month Han river commanderies and Yanzhou great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth year, seventh month: Han basin and Yanzhou underwater.

sentences.zh: 是時緣河紛爭，征戍勤瘁之應也。

translations.literal: At this time strife along the river—response of campaigning exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier armies along the Han were spent—waters rose in reply.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月甲寅，濤水入石頭，毀大航，漂船舫，有死者。

translations.literal: On jiayin day in the seventeenth year’s sixth month tidal water entered Shitou, destroyed the great bridge, swept barges—some died.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year, jiayin: Shitou tide wrecked the bridge and hulls.

sentences.zh: 京口西浦亦濤入殺人。

translations.literal: West ford at Jingkou also had tidal surge enter and kill people.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkou’s west landing drowned too.

sentences.zh: 永嘉郡潮水湧起，近海四縣人多死。

translations.literal: Yongjia commandery tide surged; four coastal counties lost many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia’s tidal bore drowned four counties.

sentences.zh: 後四年帝崩，而王恭再攻京師，京師亦發眾以禦之，兵彼頻興，百姓愁怨之應也。

translations.literal: Four years later the emperor died; Wang Gong again attacked the capital; the capital also raised hosts to resist—armies rose frequently—response of popular grief.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on the emperor fell; Wang Gong’s sieges and counter-mobilizations matched the floods.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月己亥，始興、南康、廬陵大水，深五丈。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the eighteenth year’s sixth month Shixing, Nankang, and Luling great flood—depth five zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth year, jihai: the three southern commanderies sank five zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 十九年七月，荊徐大水，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year’s seventh month Jing and Xu great flood—harmed autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth year: Jing and Xu spoiled the harvest.

sentences.zh: 二十年六月，荊徐又大水。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year’s sixth month Jing and Xu again great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Twentieth year: Jing and Xu flooded again.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月癸卯，大水。

translations.literal: On guimao day in the twenty-first year’s fifth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-first year, guimao: deluge.

sentences.zh: 是時政事多弊，兆庶非之。

translations.literal: At this time government affairs had many faults—myriad commoners condemned them.
translations.idiomatic: Policy rotted and the people muttered.

sentences.zh: 安帝五月，荊州大水，平地三丈。

translations.literal: Under Andi in the fifth month Jingzhou great flood—three zhang on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An’s fifth month sank Jingzhou ten feet deep.

sentences.zh: 去年殷仲堪舉兵向京師，是年春又殺郗恢，陰盛作威之應也。

translations.literal: The previous year Yin Zhongkan raised troops toward the capital; this spring he killed Xi Hui—response of yin flourishing and throwing weight.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan’s march on the capital and murder of Xi Hui drew the flood.

sentences.zh: 仲堪尋亦敗亡。

translations.literal: Zhongkan soon also failed and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan fell soon after.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: flood.

sentences.zh: 是時會稽王世子元顯作威陵上，又桓玄擅西夏，孫恩亂東國，陰勝陽之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Kuaiji’s heir Yuanxian lorded over superiors; moreover Huan Xuan seized western Xia, Sun En ravaged the eastern lands—response of yin overcoming yang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian bullied the throne; Huan Xuan held the west; Sun En tore the east—yin ruled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Huan Xuan usurped.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: Huan Xuan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 其明年二月庚寅夜，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: The next year’s second month gengyin night tidal water entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, gengyin night: Shitou tide.

sentences.zh: 商旅方舟萬計，漂敗流斷，骸胔相望。

translations.literal: Merchants’ paired boats counted in myriads—wreckage drifted and snapped; bones lined the banks.
translations.idiomatic: Countless merchant hulls shattered; corpses choked the shore.

sentences.zh: 江左雖頻有濤變，未有若斯之甚。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi though frequently had tidal changes, never so severe as this.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had seen surges—never this fierce.

sentences.zh: 三月，義軍克京都，玄敗走，遂夷滅之。

translations.literal: In the third month the righteous army took the capital; Xuan fled defeated and was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: loyal troops retook Jiankang; Huan Xuan fell.

sentences.zh: 三年二月己丑朔夜，濤水入石頭，漂沒殺人，大航流敗。

translations.literal: In the third year’s second month jichou new-moon night tidal water entered Shitou—drifted and drowned people; great pontoon wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, jichou night: Shitou drowned folk and ruined the bridge.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: On jiwei day in the twelfth month tidal water entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiwei: Shitou tide.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月己未夜，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: On jiwei night in the twelfth month of the second year tidal water entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, jiwei night: another Shitou surge.

sentences.zh: 明年，駱球父環潛結桓胤、殷仲文等謀作亂，劉稚亦謀反，凡所誅滅數十家。

translations.literal: The next year Luo Qiu’s father Huan secretly linked Huan Yin, Yin Zhongwen, and others plotting rebellion; Liu Zhi also rebelled—all told several tens of houses executed.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Luo Huan’s plot with Yin Zhongwen and Liu Zhi’s coup wiped dozens of families.

sentences.zh: 三年五月丙午，大水。

translations.literal: On bingwu day in the fifth month of the third year great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, fifth month, bingwu: flood.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月戊寅，濤水入石頭。

translations.literal: On wuyin day in the twelfth month of the fourth year tidal water entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, wuyin: Shitou tide.

sentences.zh: 明年，王旅北討。

translations.literal: The next year royal hosts campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial armies marched north the next year.

sentences.zh: 六年五月丁巳，大水。

translations.literal: On dingsi day in the fifth month of the sixth year great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, dingsi: deluge.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，盧循至蔡洲。

translations.literal: On yichou day Lu Xun reached Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Yichou: Lu Xun anchored at Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth year’s sixth month great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year, sixth month: flood.

sentences.zh: 九年五月辛巳，大水。

translations.literal: In the ninth year’s fifth month xinsi day great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, xinsi: flood.

sentences.zh: 十年五月丁丑，大水。

translations.literal: In the tenth year’s fifth month dingchou day great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year, dingchou: flood.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，西明門地穿，湧水出，毀門扇及限，亦水沴土也。

translations.literal: On wuyin day the west bright gate’s earth split and water gushed—destroyed doors and sills—also water encroaching on earth.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyin: Ximing Gate split open and spouted—water drowning earth.

sentences.zh: 七月乙丑，淮北風災，大水殺人。

translations.literal: On yichou day in the seventh month north of Huai wind disaster—great water killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, yichou: Huabei gale and flood.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月丙戌，大水，淹漬太廟，百官赴救。

translations.literal: On bingxu day in the eleventh year’s seventh month great flood—submerged and soaked Grand Temple—hundred officials rushed to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh year, bingxu: flood reached the temple; officials scrambled to save it.

sentences.zh: 明年，王旅北討關河。

translations.literal: The next year royal hosts campaigned north against Guan and He.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the northern expedition crossed Guanhe.

sentences.zh: 敬用五事

translations.literal: Employ the Five Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The five comportments.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「敬用五事：一曰貌，二曰言，三曰視，四曰聽，五曰思。

translations.literal: The Classic says: “Employ the five affairs: first appearance, second speech, third sight, fourth hearing, fifth thought.
translations.idiomatic: The canon lists five human gauges: bearing, words, sight, hearing, thought.

sentences.zh: 貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。

translations.literal: Appearance is called reverent; speech is called compliant; sight is called clear; hearing is called acute; thought is called perspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing must be respectful; speech obedient; vision lucid; hearing sharp; thought clear.

sentences.zh: 恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。

translations.literal: Reverence yields solemnity; compliance yields order; clarity yields wisdom; acuteness yields counsel; perspicuity yields sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: From those virtues come order, wisdom, counsel, and sage rule.

sentences.zh: 休徵：曰肅，時雨若；

translations.literal: Blessing signs: solemnity, timely rain like;
translations.idiomatic: Auspice of sobriety: seasonable rain.

sentences.zh: 乂，時晹若；

translations.literal: order, timely clearing like;
translations.idiomatic: Order brings fair skies.

sentences.zh: 哲，時燠若；

translations.literal: wisdom, timely warmth like;
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom brings gentle warmth.

sentences.zh: 謀，時寒若；

translations.literal: counsel, timely cold like;
translations.idiomatic: Counsel brings winter discipline.

sentences.zh: 聖，時風若。

translations.literal: sageliness, timely wind like.
translations.idiomatic: Sageliness brings winds in season.

sentences.zh: 咎徵：曰狂，恆雨若；

translations.literal: Ill signs: wildness, constant rain like;
translations.idiomatic: Insolence summons endless rain.

sentences.zh: 僭，恆晹若；

translations.literal: error, constant clearing like;
translations.idiomatic: Presumption brings drought glare.

sentences.zh: 豫，恆燠若；

translations.literal: hesitation, constant warmth like;
translations.idiomatic: Complacency breeds muggy heat.

sentences.zh: 急，恆寒若；

translations.literal: haste, constant cold like;
translations.idiomatic: Rashness locks the realm in cold.

sentences.zh: {雨瞀}，恆風若。」

translations.literal: {rain-haze}, constant wind like.”
translations.idiomatic: Obstruction aloft means ceaseless wind.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅，厥咎狂，厥罰恆雨，厥極惡。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: “When appearance is not reverent, this is called not solemn; its fault is wildness; its punishment constant rain; its extreme evil.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss: disrespectful bearing breaks solemnity; madness follows; endless rain is its price.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: Then there are clothing prodigies; then tortoise portents; then fowl calamities; then lower-body growing upper ailments; then green injurious signs and green auspices.
translations.idiomatic: Hence costume freaks, turtle omens, cock disasters, upside-down flesh, green blights.

sentences.zh: 惟金沴木。」

translations.literal: Only metal encroaches on wood.”
translations.idiomatic: Metal injures wood in the cycle.

sentences.zh: 說曰：凡草木之類謂之妖。

translations.literal: The explanation says: all grass-and-tree kinds are called prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Plant anomalies are called yao.

sentences.zh: 妖猶夭胎，言尚微也。

translations.literal: Prodigy is like abortion—speech says still slight.
translations.idiomatic: “Prodigy” implies incipient strangeness.

sentences.zh: 蟲豸之類謂之孽。

translations.literal: Insect-and-reptile kinds are called portents.
translations.idiomatic: Crawling things misbred are nie.

sentences.zh: 孽則芽孽矣。

translations.literal: Portent then sprouts calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Portents sprout like buds.

sentences.zh: 及六畜，謂之禍，言其著也。

translations.literal: Reaching the six domestic animals is called calamity—speech says manifest.
translations.idiomatic: When beasts show it, call it huo—clear for all to see.

sentences.zh: 及人，謂之痾。

translations.literal: Reaching humans is called ailment.
translations.idiomatic: When humans show it, call it e—malformation.

sentences.zh: 痾，病貌也，言浸深也。

translations.literal: Ailment is sick appearance—speech says gradually deepening.
translations.idiomatic: “E” marks sickness working inward.

sentences.zh: 甚則有異物生，謂之眚；

translations.literal: Extreme then strange things are born—called injurious sign;
translations.idiomatic: Extremes breed freak objects—qing calamities.

sentences.zh: 自外來，謂之祥。

translations.literal: coming from outside is called auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders bring xiang omens.

sentences.zh: 祥，猶禎也。

translations.literal: Auspice is like blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang parallels blessing.

sentences.zh: 氣相傷，謂之沴。

translations.literal: Qi harming one another is called encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: When qi wounds qi, call it li.

sentences.zh: 沴猶臨蒞，不和意也。

translations.literal: Mutually producing is called harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual sustainment is harmony.

sentences.zh: 每一事云「時則」以絕之，言非必俱至，或有或亡，或在前或在後。

translations.literal: Each affair says “in season then” to cut off—speech says not necessarily all arrive—some exist some vanish—some before some after.
translations.idiomatic: Each clause adds “when in season” to stress omens need not arrive together.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，夏侯始昌通《五經》，善推《五行傳》，以傳族子夏侯勝，下及許商，皆以教所賢弟子。

translations.literal: Under Xiaowu, Xiahou Shichang mastered the Five Classics and excelled at extending the Five Phases Tradition—transmitted to nephew Xiahou Sheng, down to Xu Shang—all taught worthy disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shichang’s cosmology passed to Xiahou Sheng and Xu Shang’s schools.

sentences.zh: 其傳與劉向同，惟劉歆傳獨異。

translations.literal: Their transmission matched Liu Xiang’s—only Liu Xin’s transmission alone differed.
translations.idiomatic: Their gloss matched Liu Xiang; Liu Xin alone diverged.

sentences.zh: 貌之不恭，是謂不肅。

translations.literal: When appearance is not reverent, this is called not solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Disrespectful bearing breaks solemnity.

sentences.zh: 肅，敬也。

translations.literal: Solemn means reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Solemnity is reverence.

sentences.zh: 內曰恭，外曰敬。

translations.literal: Within is called reverent; without is called respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Inner life shows as gong; outer shows as jing.

sentences.zh: 人君行己，體貌不恭，怠慢驕蹇，則不能敬萬事，失則狂易，故其咎狂也。

translations.literal: If the lord of men conducts himself and body and appearance are not reverent, negligent, arrogant, and proud—then he cannot reverence the myriad affairs; fault then becomes wildness—therefore its fault is wildness.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who slouch and sneer cannot honor creation—madness is their fault.

sentences.zh: 上慢下暴，則陰氣勝，故其罰常雨也。

translations.literal: Superiors slack inferiors cruel—then yin qi prevails—therefore its punishment is constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Loose thrones and cruel subjects swell yin—hence endless rain.

sentences.zh: 水傷百穀，衣食不足，則奸宄並作，故其極惡也。

translations.literal: Water harms the hundred grains—clothing and food insufficient—then treachery and villainy arise together—therefore its extreme is evil.
translations.idiomatic: Floods spoil grain; want breeds crime—that evil is the extreme.

sentences.zh: 一曰，人多被刑，或形貌醜惡，亦是也。

translations.literal: One interpretation: many people suffer punishment—or forms and faces ugly—also counts.
translations.idiomatic: Some read it as mass punishments or grotesque faces.

sentences.zh: 風俗狂慢，變節易度，則為剽輕奇怪之服，故有服妖。

translations.literal: Customs wild and slack—changing norms and shifting measures—then come flashy bizarre garments—therefore clothing prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Fashion turns reckless—odd dress follows.

sentences.zh: 水類動，故有龜孽。

translations.literal: Water kinds stir—therefore tortoise portents.
translations.idiomatic: Water forces twitch—turtle omens hatch.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《巽》為雞。

translations.literal: In the Changes Xun is chicken.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou yi maps Xun to fowl.

sentences.zh: 雞有冠、距，文武之貌。

translations.literal: Chicken has comb and spur—appearance of civil and martial.
translations.idiomatic: Cocks bear crown and spur—tokens of wen and wu.

sentences.zh: 而不為威，貌氣毀，故有雞禍。

translations.literal: Yet does not inspire awe—appearance qi ruined—therefore fowl calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Without majesty its bearing fails—hence cock disasters.

sentences.zh: 一曰，水歲多雞死及為怪，亦是也。

translations.literal: One explanation says: In years when water dominates, many chickens die and prodigious anomalies occur—this too counts.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss holds that water-phase years bring mass deaths among fowl and strange portents—and that belongs here as well.

sentences.zh: 上失威儀，則有強臣害君上者，故有下體生於上之痾。

translations.literal: When those above lose dignity of bearing, there will be powerful ministers who harm the sovereign; hence there are ailments of the lower body appearing upon the upper.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors forfeit proper bearing, strong ministers wound the ruler—which yields the prodigy of “lower members sprouting on the upper body.”

sentences.zh: 木色青，故有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: The color of wood is green; hence there are green calamities (qing sheng) and green auspices (qing xiang).
translations.idiomatic: Wood’s hue is green, which is why green blights and green omens appear.

sentences.zh: 凡貌傷者病木氣，木氣病則金沴之，沖氣相通也。

translations.literal: Generally, when bearing is impaired it sickens the qi of wood; when the qi of wood is sick, metal harms it—the clashing qi communicate with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever demeanor falters, the wood phase suffers; when wood ails, metal strikes it—the two opposing forces interact.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《震》在東方，為春為木；

translations.literal: In the Changes, Zhen lies in the east; it stands for spring and for wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes, the trigram Zhen is placed in the east—it signifies spring and wood.

sentences.zh: 《兌》在西方，為秋為金；

translations.literal: Dui lies in the west; it stands for autumn and for metal.
translations.idiomatic: Dui belongs to the west—it signifies autumn and metal.

sentences.zh: 《離》在南方，為夏為火；

translations.literal: Li lies in the south; it stands for summer and for fire.
translations.idiomatic: Li belongs to the south—it signifies summer and fire.

sentences.zh: 《坎》在北方，為冬為水。

translations.literal: Kan lies in the north; it stands for winter and for water.
translations.idiomatic: Kan belongs to the north—it signifies winter and water.

sentences.zh: 春與秋日夜分，寒暑平，是以金木之氣易以相變，故貌傷則致秋陰常雨，言傷則致春陽常旱也。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn day and night are evenly divided and cold and heat are balanced; therefore the qi of metal and wood readily transform each other; hence injury to bearing brings autumn gloom and constant rain, injury to speech brings spring sunshine and constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn balance day and night and level cold with heat, so metal and wood readily trade influence—thus impaired bearing yields endless autumn rains, while impaired speech yields spring drought beneath a glaring sun.

sentences.zh: 至於冬夏，日夜相反，寒暑殊絕，水火之氣不得相並，故視傷常燠、聽傷常寒者，其氣然也。

translations.literal: As for winter and summer, day and night are opposed and cold and heat are utterly different; the qi of water and fire cannot stand together; hence injury to sight brings constant warmth and injury to hearing brings constant cold—their qi are thus.
translations.idiomatic: Winter and summer invert day and night and separate cold from heat so sharply that water and fire cannot mingle—so impaired sight trends warm and impaired hearing trends cold: that is how their phases behave.

sentences.zh: 逆之，其極曰惡；

translations.literal: If one opposes it, its culmination is called “evil.”
translations.idiomatic: Defy the pattern, and the extreme is named evil.

sentences.zh: 順之，其福曰攸好德。

translations.literal: If one follows it, its blessing is called “that fondness for virtue.”
translations.idiomatic: Follow it, and the blessing is “delight in virtue.”

sentences.zh: 劉歆《貌傳》曰有鱗蟲之孽，羊禍，鼻痾。

translations.literal: Liu Xin’s “Treatise on Bearing” says there are calamities of scale-covered creatures, sheep disasters, and ailments of the nose.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin’s Treatise on Bearing lists prodigies among scaly creatures, sheep omens, and nasal deformities.

sentences.zh: 說以為于天文東方辰為龍星，故為鱗蟲。

translations.literal: The explanation holds that in astrology the eastern chen is the Dragon Star; hence they count as scale-covered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss identifies the eastern asterism chen as the Dragon Star—hence “scaly creatures.”

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《兌》為羊，木為金所病，故致羊禍，與常雨同應。

translations.literal: In the Changes, Dui represents sheep; wood is overcome by metal; hence it brings sheep disasters, responding together with constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changes Dui signifies sheep; wood falls ill to metal—hence sheep calamities that align with ceaseless rain.

sentences.zh: 此說非是。

translations.literal: This explanation is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: That reading is wrong.

sentences.zh: 春與秋氣陰陽相敵，木病金盛，故能相並，惟此一事耳。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn yin and yang are evenly matched; wood is sick and metal prevails; hence they can interact—only in this one case.
translations.idiomatic: Only in spring and autumn do yin and yang contend as equals, with enfeebled wood under dominant metal, so the phases can combine—nowhere else.

sentences.zh: 禍與妖痾祥眚同類，不得獨異。

translations.literal: Disasters belong with prodigies, ailments, auspices, and calamities of the same kind; they cannot be treated as uniquely different.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities sit on the same spectrum as prodigies, lesions, omens, and blights—you cannot set them apart.

sentences.zh: 魏尚書鄧颺揚行步馳縱，筋不束體，坐起傾倚，若無手足，此貌之不恭也。

translations.literal: Among Wei, Minister Deng Yang’s gait was reckless and unbridled, sinews failing to bind his frame; sitting or rising he leaned and tilted as if he had no hands or feet—this was irreverence of bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang of Wei, a Secretariat director, walked with a loose, racing stride—his sinews seemed not to hold his body; he slumped when he sat or rose as though limbless: irreverence of demeanor.

sentences.zh: 管輅謂之鬼躁。

translations.literal: Guan Lu called it “ghost agitation.”
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu dubbed it “demon restlessness.”

sentences.zh: 鬼躁者，凶終之徵，後卒誅也。

translations.literal: “Ghost agitation” is a portent of a violent end; later he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: “Ghost restlessness” foretells a bloody finish—he was put to death in the end.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康中，貴遊子弟相與為散發倮身之飲，對弄婢妾，逆之者傷好，非之者負譏，希世之士恥不與焉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui’s Yuan-kang era, noble youths together held drinking parties with hair loosened and bodies bare, sporting with concubine-maids before one another; whoever opposed them injured friendships, whoever criticized them bore ridicule, and men seeking fame were ashamed not to join.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui in the Yuan-kang years, young aristocrats threw banquets with hair unbound and skins naked, fondling servant girls in plain sight; crossing them cost goodwill, criticizing them earned jeers, and career-minded men were ashamed to stay away.

sentences.zh: 蓋貌之不恭，胡狄侵中國之萌也。

translations.literal: This was irreverence of bearing—the first sprouting of northern tribes invading the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: It was bearing without dignity—the first stirrings of steppe peoples overrunning China.

sentences.zh: 其後遂有五胡之亂，此又失在狂也。

translations.literal: Afterward there came the turmoil of the Five Hu—this again lay in the fault called frenzy.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Hu upheaval followed—another case of the “madness” failing.

sentences.zh: 元康中，賈謐親貴，數入二宮，與儲君遊戲，無降下心。

translations.literal: In Yuan-kang, Jia Mi was honored as kin, entered the two inner palaces repeatedly, and played games with the heir apparent, showing no mind of submission.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuan-kang, Jia Mi enjoyed imperial favor: he kept slipping into the two palaces to amuse the crown prince and never lowered himself in deference.

sentences.zh: 又嘗因弈棋爭道，成都王穎厲色曰：「皇太子國之儲貳，賈謐何敢無禮！

translations.literal: Moreover he once quarreled over a weiqi move; the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, said sternly: “The imperial heir is the nation’s successor—how dare Jia Mi be rude!
translations.idiomatic: Once, disputing a chess placement, Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, snapped: “The crown prince is the realm’s reserve—how dare Jia Mi lack respect!

sentences.zh: 」謐猶不悛，故及於禍，貌不恭之罰也。

translations.literal: ” Jia Mi still did not reform, hence he met disaster—the punishment for irreverence of bearing.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet Jia Mi refused to mend his ways and paid with his life—the reckoning for disrespectful bearing.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏既誅趙王倫，因留輔政，坐拜百官，符敕臺府，淫醟專驕，不一朝覲，此狂恣不肅之咎也。

translations.literal: Prince Qi, Sima Jiong, having executed Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, remained to assist governance: seated he invested the hundred officials, issued edicts from terrace offices, drowned in wine and sole arrogance, and never once attended court—this was the fault of mad presumption and want of solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Prince Qi Sima Jiong stayed as regent: he handed out posts from his seat, ran the ministries by decree, reveled in wine and pride, and skipped every audience—mad impudence with no dignity.

sentences.zh: 天下莫不高其功而慮其亡也，冏終弗改，遂致夷滅。

translations.literal: None under Heaven failed to honor his merit yet dread his ruin; Jiong to the end did not reform, and so met extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The realm praised his deed yet feared his fall; Jiong never changed—and was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 司馬道子於府園內列肆，使姬人酤鬻，身自貿易。

translations.literal: Sima Daozi set out market stalls in his manor garden, had concubines sell ale, and traded in person.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi lined his estate with shops, put concubines behind the counter, and haggled himself.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為貴者失位，降在皁隸之象也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao took it as the image of the noble losing position and descending among dark-clad servants.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao read it as rank pulled down among common hirelings.

sentences.zh: 俄而道子見廢，以庶人終，此貌不恭之應也。

translations.literal: Soon Daozi was deposed and ended as a commoner—this responded to irreverence of bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was soon stripped of office and died a commoner—the sign answering irreverent bearing.

sentences.zh: 安帝，將拜授劉毅世子，毅以王命之重，當設饗宴，親請吏佐臨視。

translations.literal: Emperor An, about to invest Liu Yi’s son as heir, Liu Yi—because the royal command was weighty—ought to have laid a feast and personally invited clerks to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An was to ennoble Liu Yi’s heir, Liu Yi—because the imperial commission mattered—should have spread a banquet and brought his staff to witness it.

sentences.zh: 至拜日，國僚不重白，默拜於廄中。

translations.literal: On the day of investiture, his household colleagues did not report upward again; they silently performed the rite in the stable.
translations.idiomatic: Come the ceremony, his officers never cleared it upstairs; they muttered the investiture inside the stables.

sentences.zh: 王人將反命，毅方知之，大以為恨，免郎中令劉敬叔官。

translations.literal: When the king’s envoy was about to return his report, Liu Yi only then learned of it, greatly resented it, and dismissed Director of Gentlemen of the Palace Liu Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial messenger was nearly on the road back before Liu Yi heard—he was furious and cashiered Liu Jingshu, director of the gentlemen-of-the-palace.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，此惰略嘉禮不肅之妖也。

translations.literal: Heaven’s warning seemed to say: this was the prodigy of lazily slighting a splendid rite and lacking solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned: skimping on a sacred ceremony without gravity yields this portent.

sentences.zh: 其後毅遂被殺焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Yi was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was executed soon after.

sentences.zh: 庶征恆雨，劉歆以為《春秋》大雨，劉向以為大水。

translations.literal: Among the miscellaneous signs, constant rain—Liu Xin took it as “great rain” in the Spring and Autumn; Liu Xiang as “great flood.”
translations.idiomatic: Under “miscellaneous omens,” endless rain: Liu Xin reads the Spring and Autumn’s “great rains”; Liu Xiang reads catastrophic flood.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝秋，數大雨，多暴卒，雷電非常，至殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: In Wei Mingdi’s autumn it rained heavily many times; many died suddenly; thunder and lightning were extraordinary, even killing birds.
translations.idiomatic: One autumn under Wei’s Mingdi the skies opened repeatedly; people dropped dead; lightning flashed unnaturally, killing even small birds.

sentences.zh: 案楊阜上疏，此恆雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Yang Fu’s memorial, this was the punishment of constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu’s memorial treats it as the scourge of ceaseless rain.

sentences.zh: 時天子居喪不哀，出入弋獵無度，奢侈繁興，奪農時，故水失其性而恆雨為罰。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven in mourning was not mournful, went out and in hunting without limit, luxury flourished in profusion, and farming seasons were seized; hence water lost its nature and constant rain served as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore mourning without grief, hunted without restraint, lavished wealth, and stole time from the fields—water lost its proper character, and unending rain was the penalty.

sentences.zh: 八月，大雨霖三十餘日，伊、洛、河、漢皆溢，歲以凶饑。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, great rain fell more than thirty days; the Yi, Luo, Yellow River, and Han all overflowed; the year saw famine.
translations.idiomatic: For over thirty days in the eighth month torrents fell; the Yi, Luo, Yellow River, and Han burst their banks; the harvest failed and hunger spread.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮二月甲寅，大雨，震電。

translations.literal: Wu’s Sun Liang, second month, day jiayin: great rain, thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin of the second month under Wu’s Sun Liang came deluges and lightning.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，雪，大寒。

translations.literal: Yimao: snow, great cold.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, yimao: snow and bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆說，此時當雨而不當大，大雨，恆雨之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xin’s doctrine, at this season it ought to rain but not heavily; heavy rain is the punishment of constant rain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin argues it should have sprinkled then—a deluge instead marks the “constant rain” scourge.

sentences.zh: 於始震電之，明日而雪，大寒，又常寒之罰也。

translations.literal: At first thunder and lightning; the next day snow, great cold—again the punishment of constant cold.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning first, then snow and killing frost the day after—another stroke of “constant cold.”

sentences.zh: 劉向以為既已雷電，則雪不當復降，皆失時之異也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that once there had been thunder and lightning, snow ought not to fall again—all were anomalies of mistimed seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang thought lightning should rule out more snow—each event arrived out of season.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，為君失時，賊臣將起。

translations.literal: Heaven’s warning seemed to say: the ruler loses the seasons; traitorous ministers will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned: mistiming sovereignty breeds rebellious ministers.

sentences.zh: 先震電而後雪者，陰見間隙，起而勝陽，逆弑之禍將成也。

translations.literal: Thunder and lightning first and snow afterward means yin saw an opening, rose, and overcame yang—the disaster of usurpation and regicide will take shape.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning then snow means yin spied a gap, surged, and mastered yang—the blade and coup draw near.

sentences.zh: 亮不悟，尋見廢。

translations.literal: Liang did not understand; soon he was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang never saw it—soon he was cast down.

sentences.zh: 此與《春秋》魯隱同。

translations.literal: This matches Duke Yin of Lu in the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: It parallels the Spring and Autumn record for Duke Yin of Lu.

sentences.zh: 武帝六月，大雨霖。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, sixth month: great soaking rain.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu’s sixth month the rains would not stop.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，河、洛、伊、沁水同時並溢，流四千九百餘家，殺二百餘人，沒秋稼千三百六十餘頃。

translations.literal: Jiachen: the Yellow River, Luo, Yi, and Qin streams overflowed together, swept four thousand nine hundred-odd households, killed two hundred-odd people, and submerged autumn crops over thirteen hundred sixty qing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Yellow River, Luo, Yi, and Qin floods crested as one, washing away nearly five thousand homes, killing over two hundred, and drowning more than 1,360 qing of autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 七月，任城、梁國暴雨，害豆麥。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Ren-cheng and Liang-nation violent rain, harming beans and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Ren-cheng and Liang were hit by cloudbursts that ruined beans and wheat.

sentences.zh: 九月，南安郡霖雨暴雪，樹木摧折，害秋稼。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Nan-an commandery unending rain and violent snow; trees snapped; autumn crops were harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Nan-an commandery endured weeks of rain and blizzard that shattered trees and spoiled the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 是秋，魏郡西平郡九縣、淮南、平原霖雨暴水，霜傷秋稼。

translations.literal: That autumn, nine counties of Wei commandery and Xi-ping commandery, Huai-nan, and Ping-yuan saw soaking rain and sudden floods; frost injured autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: That fall, nine counties across Wei and Xi-ping along with Huai-nan and Ping-yuan were flooded; late frost ruined the crops.

sentences.zh: 惠帝十月、義陽、南陽、東海霖雨，淹害秋麥。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui, tenth month: Yi-yang, Nan-yang, and Dong-hai soaking rain, inundating and harming autumn wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui’s tenth month relentless rain swamped Yi-yang, Nan-yang, and Dong-hai and drowned the winter wheat.

sentences.zh: 元帝，春雨至於夏。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan: spring rain lasting into summer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan spring rains dragged into summer.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦執權，不恭之罰也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun held power—the punishment of irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun held the reins then—the penalty for irreverent bearing.

sentences.zh: ，春雨四十餘日，晝夜雷電震五十餘日。

translations.literal: , Spring rain lasted more than forty days; day and night thunder and lightning shook for more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: For over forty days spring rains fell; thunder rolled night and day for more than fifty.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦興兵，王師敗績之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun raised troops—this responded to the defeat of the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was marching then—the omen of the imperial army’s rout.

sentences.zh: 成帝，春雨五十餘日，恆雷電。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng: spring rain more than fifty days, constant thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng’s reign brought fifty-odd days of spring rain and ceaseless thunder.

sentences.zh: 是時雖斬蘇峻，其餘黨猶據守石頭，至其滅後，淫雨乃霽。

translations.literal: At this time although Su Jun had been beheaded, his remaining partisans still held Stone Citadel; only after they were extinguished did the excessive rain clear.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun was dead but his followers still held Stone City; only when they were wiped out did the endless rain break.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，荊州之長沙攸、醴陵、武陵之龍陽，三縣雨水，浮漂屋室，殺人，損秋稼。

translations.literal: Eighth month, yichou: You county (Chang-sha), Li-ling, and Long-yang (Wu-ling)—three counties’ rainwater floated houses, killed people, and harmed autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the eighth month, downpours in You (Chang-sha), Li-ling, and Long-yang (Wu-ling) swept away homes, took lives, and ruined the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 是時帝幼，權在於下。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was young; power lay below.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was a child; real power sat beneath the throne.

translations.literal: Equals sign used as a typographical section divider.
translations.idiomatic: Typographical section divider.

sentences.zh: 服妖

translations.literal: Clothing prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Garment omens.

sentences.zh: =魏武帝以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，始擬古皮弁，裁縑帛為白帢，以易舊服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei, because all under Heaven suffered famine and goods were scarce, first imitated the ancient leather cap, cutting silk tabby to make a white qia in place of the former dress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei, with the realm starving and supplies exhausted, copied the old leather bonnet and tailored plain silk into a white qia to replace court headgear.

sentences.zh: 傅玄曰；

translations.literal: Fu Xuan said;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan observed:

sentences.zh: 「白乃軍容，非國容也。

translations.literal: “White is military dress, not court dress.
translations.idiomatic: “White belongs on campaign, not in state ritual.

sentences.zh: 」干寶以為「縞素，凶喪之象也」。

translations.literal: ” Gan Bao held that “plain white silk is the image of death and mourning.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Gan Bao read it as “bleached cloth signals bereavement.”

sentences.zh: 名之為帢，毀辱之言也，蓋革代之後，劫殺之妖也。

translations.literal: Naming it qia is language of insult and ruin; after the change of mandate it was the prodigy of robbery and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it a qia was mockery—a portent of usurpation and bloodshed after the throne changed hands.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝著繡帽，披縹紈半袖，常以見直臣楊阜，諫曰：「此禮何法服邪！

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi wore an embroidered cap and draped a half-sleeve of sky-blue tabby; he often wore it to audience the upright minister Yang Fu, who remonstrated: “What ritual norm of dress is this!
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi of Wei sported an embroidered hat and a sky-blue half-sleeve; he wore them to see the upright Yang Fu, who protested: “What canonical garment is this!

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: ” The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor had no reply.

sentences.zh: 近服妖也。

translations.literal: This bordered on clothing prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: It skirted a garment omen.

sentences.zh: 夫縹，非禮之色。

translations.literal: Now sky-blue is not a color sanctioned by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Sky-blue is not a ritual hue.

sentences.zh: 褻服尚不以紅紫，況接臣下乎？

translations.literal: Even intimate garments do not use red and purple—how much more when receiving ministers below?
translations.idiomatic: Undress eschews forbidden reds and purples—how dare court robes flout them before ministers?

sentences.zh: 人主親禦非法之章，所謂自作孽不可禳也。

translations.literal: The ruler personally assumes unlawful insignia—what is called self-made calamity cannot be expiated.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign dons unlawful regalia, he courts a doom no rite can lift.

sentences.zh: 帝既不享永年，身沒而祿去王室，後嗣不終，遂亡天下。

translations.literal: The emperor did not enjoy long years; his person gone and stipends departed from the royal house, posterity did not reach its term, and so all under Heaven was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He gained no long reign; dead, his line lost the mandate—his heirs did not endure, and the realm slipped away.

sentences.zh: ，發銅鑄為巨人二，號曰翁仲，置之司馬門外。

translations.literal: , They melted copper to cast two giants, called them Wengzhong, and placed them outside the Sima Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze was recast into two colossal statues dubbed Wengzhong and set outside the Sima Gate.

sentences.zh: 案古長人見，為國亡。

translations.literal: According to antiquity, when tall men appear, it is for the state’s perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient precedent says giants foretell a kingdom’s end.

sentences.zh: 長狄見臨洮，為秦亡之禍。

translations.literal: The Long Di appeared at Lintao—disaster for Qin’s perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Long Di at Lintao spelled Qin’s doom.

sentences.zh: 始皇不悟，反以為嘉祥，鑄銅人以象之。

translations.literal: The First Emperor did not understand; instead he took it as auspicious omen and cast bronze men to image them.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor misread the sign as blessing and cast bronze giants in their likeness.

sentences.zh: 魏法亡國之器，而於義竟無取焉。

translations.literal: Wei copied the device of a perishing state, and in rectitude it ultimately took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei copied a dying dynasty’s stunt—to no moral purpose.

sentences.zh: 蓋服妖也。

translations.literal: This was clothing prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Another garment omen.

sentences.zh: 尚書何晏好服婦人之服，傅玄曰：「此妖服也。

translations.literal: Minister He Yan liked to wear women’s dress; Fu Xuan said: “This is prodigy dress.
translations.idiomatic: Director He Yan favored women’s clothing; Fu Xuan said: “This is omen dress.

sentences.zh: 夫衣裳之制，所以定上下殊內外也。

translations.literal: The system of upper and lower garments is how one fixes superiors and inferiors and distinguishes inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: Robes exist to set high against low and inside against outside.

sentences.zh: 《大雅》云『玄袞赤舄，鉤膺鏤錫』，歌其文也。

translations.literal: The Greater Odes says, “Dark robe and red shoes, hooked breastplate and carved bells”—it sings its pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Odes exclaims “black robe, red slippers, hooked breast-straps, chased bells”—praising its ornament.

sentences.zh: 《小雅》云『有嚴有翼，共武之服』，詠其武也。

translations.literal: The Lesser Odes says, “Awesome and aiding, together in martial dress”—it chants its martial quality.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Odes cries “solemn, supportive—those martial robes together”—honoring their strength.

sentences.zh: 若內外不殊，王制失敘，服妖既作，身隨之亡。

translations.literal: If inner and outer are not distinguished, royal regulation loses order; once clothing prodigy arises, the person follows it in death.
translations.idiomatic: Blur inner with outer and royal order collapses; garment omens appear—and the wearer perishes.

sentences.zh: 妹嬉冠男子之冠，桀亡天下；

translations.literal: Mo Xi capped herself with a man’s cap—Jie lost all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Mo Xi wore a man’s crown—Jie lost the realm;

sentences.zh: 何晏服婦人之服，亦亡其家，其咎均也。」

translations.literal: He Yan wore women’s dress—also lost his family; the fault is equal.”
translations.idiomatic: He Yan dressed as a woman—and lost his house; the guilt matches.”

sentences.zh: 吳婦人修容者，急束其發而劘角過於耳，蓋其俗自操束太急，而廉隅失中之謂也。

translations.literal: Among Wu women who adorned their faces, they tightly bound their hair and shaved the temples past the ears—this speaks of their custom binding itself too tight and of corners losing the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Wu women who styled their looks wrenched their hair tight and cropped temples past the ears—vanity pulled so taut that proportion broke.

sentences.zh: 故吳之風俗，相驅以急，言論彈射，以刻薄相尚。
